contracts.contract_plain_english: For any positive k and finite floating-point inputs with b_k nonzero, evaluating (c-sum a_i b_i)/b_k in round-to-nearest arithmetic, in any summation-tree order and without underflow or overflow, yields a computed y_hat that satisfies an exact coefficientwise backward identity with c unchanged and every coefficient bounded by k*u. [PDF p. 10, printed p. 693; anchor: Lemma 4.1 statement; PDF p. 3, printed p. 686; anchor: whatever-order and unperturbed-c discussion] If b_k=1, every bound is (k-1)u, and the proof constructs sign-aligned witnesses from one scalar residual epsilon. [PDF p. 10, printed p. 693; anchor: Lemma 4.1 proof] The constants contain no O(u^2) term and require no smallness condition on k*u. [PDF p. 10, printed p. 693; anchor: subsection 4.1 opening paragraph]

source_evidence.observation: For positive k, floating-point a_1,...,a_{k-1}, b_1,...,b_k, c with b_k nonzero, the computed value y_hat of (c-sum a_i b_i)/b_k admits coefficients theta_k^(0),...,theta_k^(k-1) satisfying the displayed exact identity and absolute bounds ku; when b_k=1, all bounds improve to (k-1)u.

For b_k=1, the proof first bounds |y_hat-y| by (k-1)u times |y_hat| plus the absolute product sum, represents the residual using one real epsilon, and defines epsilon^(0)=-sign(y_hat)epsilon and epsilon^(i)=-sign(a_i b_i)epsilon.
The paper interprets whatever order as any rooted binary summation tree over c and the product terms; it also emphasizes that c remains unperturbed in these backward identities.

The improved bounds are stated to have no dimension restriction and no quadratic terms, and to hold for round-to-nearest arithmetic with any radix, tie-breaking rule, and summation order when underflow and overflow are absent.

contracts.contract_plain_english: For a floating-point m-by-n matrix with m>=n, completed Gaussian elimination without underflow or overflow produces computed factors satisfying the exact backward equation L_hat U_hat=A+DeltaA and the componentwise bound |DeltaA|<=n*u*|L_hat||U_hat|. [PDF p. 10, printed p. 693; anchor: Theorem 4.2] In the square case the bound sharpens rowwise to diag((i-1)u)|L_hat||U_hat| and globally to (n-1)u|L_hat||U_hat|. [PDF p. 10, printed p. 693; anchor: equation (4.2)] The Doolittle proof preserves two distinct local coefficients, (k-1)u for row-k U updates and k*u for below-diagonal column-k L updates, and obtains the square result from k*u<=(i-1)u<=(n-1)u. [PDF p. 11, printed p. 694; anchor: equations (4.3a)-(4.3b) and final comparison] These are componentwise, O(u^2)-free bounds with no n*u<1 restriction. [PDF p. 4, printed p. 687; anchor: improved-bound discussion]

statement.algorithm_linkage: The theorem is stated for Gaussian elimination generally. The proof analyzes the Doolittle schedule: at step k it computes row k of U_hat by subtraction updates, sets L_hat_kk=1, and computes the below-diagonal part of column k of L_hat by subtraction followed by division by U_hat_kk. The paper says this suffices because the formulations are mathematically equivalent, and the local estimates hold for any summation order. The off-diagonal upper-triangle residual has coefficient i u for i<j, while the diagonal residual has coefficient (j+1)u.

source_evidence.observation: The proof obtains the full componentwise conclusion from the symmetry of A-R_hat^T R_hat and R_hat^T R_hat.
diag(f(i)) denotes the n x n diagonal matrix with entries f(i) and implicit index range i=1,...,n.

statement.algorithm_linkage: The theorem is tied to the conventional unpivoted, upper-triangular, columnwise Cholesky method: column j computes each R_hat_ij by a subtraction followed by division by R_hat_ii and computes R_hat_jj from a subtraction followed by a square root. Lemmas 4.1 and 4.3 yield the two local bounds, and symmetry extends them from the computed upper triangle to the full residual. [PDF p. 11, printed p. 694; anchor: Section 4.3 setup and Lemma 4.3; PDF p. 12, printed p. 695; anchor: update formulas, equations (4.5), and symmetry sentence]
binders: n is the matrix dimension and A belongs to F^(n x n). [PDF p. 11, printed p. 694; anchor: Theorem 4.4 statement]
R_hat belongs to F^(n x n) and is the computed Cholesky factor. [PDF p. 11, printed p. 694; anchor: Theorem 4.4 statement]
For the local estimates, j=1,...,n; equation (4.5a) uses i=1,...,j-1, and equation (4.5b) concerns the diagonal index j. [PDF p. 12, printed p. 695; anchor: equations (4.5a)-(4.5b)]
conclusions: R_hat^T*R_hat = A+DeltaA exactly. [PDF p. 12, printed p. 695; anchor: equation (4.4)]
|DeltaA| <= diag((i+1)u)*|R_hat^T|*|R_hat| <= (n+1)u*|R_hat^T|*|R_hat| componentwise. [PDF p. 12, printed p. 695; anchor: equation (4.4)]
For 1<=i<j<=n, |a_ij-sum_{k=1}^{i} R_hat_ki R_hat_kj| <= i*u*sum_{k=1}^{i}|R_hat_ki||R_hat_kj|. [PDF p. 12, printed p. 695; anchor: equation (4.5a)]
For j=1,...,n, |a_jj-sum_{k=1}^{j} R_hat_kj^2| <= (j+1)u*sum_{k=1}^{j}R_hat_kj^2. [PDF p. 12, printed p. 695; anchor: equation (4.5b)]

The bounds obtained directly for the computed upper triangle extend to the full matrix because A-R_hat^T R_hat and R_hat^T R_hat are symmetric. [PDF p. 12, printed p. 695; anchor: closing symmetry sentence]
constants_and_indexing: The rowwise theorem coefficient is (i+1)u for i=1,...,n, and its uniform maximum is (n+1)u. [PDF p. 9, printed p. 692; anchor: diag notation; PDF p. 12, printed p. 695; anchor: equation (4.4)]
The off-diagonal local coefficient is i*u for 1<=i<j, with sums through k=i. [PDF p. 12, printed p. 695; anchor: equation (4.5a)]
The diagonal local coefficient is (j+1)u, with sums through k=j. [PDF p. 12, printed p. 695; anchor: equation (4.5b)]
The first row of the rowwise matrix bound has coefficient 2u, not u or zero. [PDF p. 9, printed p. 692; anchor: diag index convention; PDF p. 12, printed p. 695; anchor: equation (4.4)]
definitions_and_conventions: In the preceding setup, the exact Cholesky factor of a real symmetric positive-definite A is the unique upper-triangular R with positive diagonal satisfying A=R^T R; Cholesky factorization means computation by the conventional algorithm. [PDF p. 11, printed p. 694; anchor: Section 4.3 opening paragraph]
At column j, the off-diagonal expression is y_ij=(a_ij-sum_{k=1}^{i-1}R_hat_ki R_hat_kj)/R_hat_ii for i=1,...,j-1. [PDF p. 12, printed p. 695; anchor: columnwise Cholesky update formulas]
The diagonal expression is y_jj=(a_jj-sum_{k=1}^{j-1}R_hat_kj^2)^(1/2). [PDF p. 12, printed p. 695; anchor: columnwise Cholesky update formulas]
R_hat_ij and R_hat_jj are the computed floating-point values of those expressions. [PDF p. 12, printed p. 695; anchor: paragraph preceding equations (4.5)]
diag((i+1)u) acts on the left and is therefore a rowwise coefficient with i=1,...,n. [PDF p. 9, printed p. 692; anchor: diag notation; PDF p. 12, printed p. 695; anchor: equation (4.4)]

DeltaA is the exact perturbation R_hat^T R_hat-A; the products in (4.4)-(4.5) are mathematical products of computed entries, not a separately rounded matrix multiplication. [PDF p. 12, printed p. 695; anchor: equations (4.4)-(4.5)]
error_notions: DeltaA is a componentwise backward error in the exact identity R_hat^T R_hat=A+DeltaA. [PDF p. 12, printed p. 695; anchor: equation (4.4)]
Equation (4.5a) is an off-diagonal absolute residual bound and equation (4.5b) is a diagonal absolute residual bound. [PDF p. 12, printed p. 695; anchor: equations (4.5a)-(4.5b)]
The full bound is obtained by symmetry rather than by separately analyzing lower-triangular update operations. [PDF p. 12, printed p. 695; anchor: closing symmetry sentence]
exceptional_values: Underflow and overflow are excluded. [PDF p. 11, printed p. 694; anchor: Theorem 4.4 statement]

The theorem conditions on the algorithm running to completion; the square-root lemma used in its proof requires a nonnegative computed radicand. [PDF p. 11, printed p. 694; anchor: Lemma 4.3 and Theorem 4.4]

The theorem does not explicitly require A to be positive definite, nor does it separately state strict positivity of every computed diagonal entry. [PDF p. 11, printed p. 694; anchor: contrast between Section 4.3 setup and Theorem 4.4]
higher_order_terms: The bounds contain no added O(u^2) term. [PDF p. 4, printed p. 687; anchor: improved-bound discussion; PDF p. 12, printed p. 695; anchor: equation (4.4)]
No restriction such as (n+1)u<1 is present. [PDF p. 4, printed p. 687; anchor: no-dimension-restriction discussion; PDF p. 11, printed p. 694; anchor: Theorem 4.4]
hypotheses: A is symmetric; positive definiteness is not an explicit hypothesis of Theorem 4.4. [PDF p. 11, printed p. 694; anchor: Theorem 4.4 statement]
Cholesky factorization runs to completion. [PDF p. 11, printed p. 694; anchor: Theorem 4.4 statement]
No underflow or overflow occurs. [PDF p. 11, printed p. 694; anchor: Theorem 4.4 statement]

The proof uses the conventional columnwise upper-triangular algorithm and permits any order for evaluating its sums. [PDF p. 12, printed p. 695; anchor: columnwise update formulas and paragraph preceding (4.5)]
implicit_context: The positive-definite discussion defines the usual Cholesky object, but the theorem deliberately states the conditional result for any symmetric floating-point A on which the algorithm completes. [PDF p. 11, printed p. 694; anchor: Section 4.3 setup and Theorem 4.4]

Lemma 4.3 supplies the diagonal square-root estimate when its computed radicand is nonnegative; Lemma 4.1 supplies the off-diagonal division estimate. [PDF p. 11, printed p. 694; anchor: Lemma 4.3 and transition to Theorem 4.4; PDF p. 12, printed p. 695; anchor: application preceding (4.5)]

The standing arithmetic is round to nearest with arbitrary radix and tie-breaking rule. [PDF p. 4, printed p. 687; anchor: discussion following equation (1.8); PDF p. 5, printed p. 688; anchor: Section 2.1]
norms: No matrix or vector norm is used; scalar bars are absolute values, matrix bars are entrywise absolute values, and the inequalities are componentwise. [PDF p. 12, printed p. 695; anchor: equations (4.4)-(4.5)]
numerical_model: A and R_hat have entries in F, with round-to-nearest arithmetic and u=(1/2)beta^(1-p). [PDF p. 5, printed p. 688; anchor: Sections 2.1-2.2; PDF p. 11, printed p. 694; anchor: Theorem 4.4]
The result allows arbitrary radix, tie breaking, dimension, and summation order. [PDF p. 4, printed p. 687; anchor: discussion following equation (1.8)]
Underflow and overflow are excluded, but no condition (n+1)u<1 is imposed. [PDF p. 11, printed p. 694; anchor: Theorem 4.4; PDF p. 4, printed p. 687; anchor: no-restriction discussion]
